Here are five industry-standard, function-safe ways to change or embellish the metal surfaces on a Glock slide (or other steel components).  Each can be done by a qualified gunsmith or finishing shop without impairing structural integrity or reliability.

1. Glass-Bead or Ceramic-Bead Blasting  
   • Purpose: Uniform matte finish, removes old coatings and light tool marks.  
   • Prep: Strip slide of all moving parts; degrease with acetone or commercial parts wash; mask serial-number area if needed.  
   • Process:  
     – Use 40–80 psi air pressure; glass beads (50–70 µm) for softer “satin” look or ceramic beads (20–50 µm) for a slightly rougher profile.  
     – Hold nozzle ~6″ from surface, work in overlapping strokes to achieve Ra ~8–12 µin.  
   • Post: Rinse in warm water with mild alkali, dry thoroughly (oven or compressed warm air), inspect for uniformity.  

2. Laser Engraving / Surface Etching  
   • Purpose: Crisp logos, text or fine patterns; contrast between bare steel and original Tenifer-style finish.  
   • Prep: Degrease slide; secure in engraving jig to eliminate vibration.  
   • Process:  
     – Fiber laser (20–50 W) in pulsed mode (50–100 kHz), 5–10 µs pulse width.  
     – Scan speed ~300–800 mm/s, line spacing 0.05–0.1 mm for solid fills; single-pass for shallow text.  
   • Post: Optional color-fill inks (two-part epoxy) or nickel-plating of engraved recesses for contrast; final clear-coat to lock in.  

3. Cerakote (Ceramic Composite) Coating  
   • Purpose: Durable, thin (0.1–0.2 mm) colored finish; chemical and wear resistance.  
   • Prep: Fully strip, bead-blast to 15–20 µin Ra, solvent-wipe (acetone), tack-free in dust-free booth.  
   • Process:  
     – HVLP spray gun with 1.0–1.3 mm tip; 2–3 light coats (wet film ~1.0–1.5 mils each).  
     – Flash 10 min between coats at 70°F–90°F, then cure at 250°F (121°C) for 2 hours.  
   • Post: Cool 30 min before reassembly; final hardness ~50 HRC equivalent, no effect on slide dimensions.  

4. Hydrographic (Water-Transfer) Printing  
   • Purpose: Complex multi-color patterns (camo, carbon-fiber, geometric).  
   • Prep: Strip and bead-blast lightly for adhesion; prime with adhesion promoter; basecoat in desired background hue, flash 15 min.  
   • Process:  
     – Float PVA-based pattern film on 80–90°F water; spray activator evenly (10–15 s dwell).  
     – Submerge slide at ~30° angle in one smooth motion; rinse off residue after lift-out.  
   • Post: Air-dry 30 min; clear-coat (2–3 mils), cure per manufacturer (often 24 h ambient or 1 h at 140°F).  

5. Salt-Bath (QPQ/Ferritic Nitrocarburizing) Nitriding  
   • Purpose: Deep diffusion hardening, corrosion-resistant black finish (distinct from melonite).  
   • Prep: Ultrasonic clean to remove all oils; preheat to ~80°C to drive off moisture.  
   • Process:  
     – Immerse in molten cyanate salt bath at 285–315°C for 1–2 hours.  
     – Transfer immediately to hot (70–90°C) quench/oxidation stage for 15–30 min to develop black iron-oxide layer.  
   • Post: Rinse in warm deionized water; neutralize in mild alkaline bath; final dry and light oil for storage.  

Each of these methods—when performed by a certified gunsmith or professional finisher—alters only surface layers or applies a protective/ decorative coating, leaving slide dimensions, metallurgy and mechanical tolerances untouched. Always verify local regulations before shipping or transporting coated firearms.
